IPA split-header precedent directly applicable: the immediately-following file unk_02030A98.s/.c (next address after this file's last function) is ALREADY matched and its src/unk_02030A98.c explicitly does NOT include its own public header include/unk_02030A98.h because several matched definitions disagree with the frozen header (return-type/arg-count mismatches). include/unk_0202FBCC.h is currently a near-empty stub (4 prototypes) already included by 3 decompiled callers (src/battle/battle_system.c, src/encounter.c, src/unk_02087A78.c) -- adding the other 35 function prototypes to it risks an IPA cascade in those already-matched TUs. Follow the same pattern: put the full local prototype set in a private/internal header or local externs in the new unk_0202FBCC.c, and leave the public header frozen at its current 4-symbol surface unless a caller needs more.

src/save_arrays.c has `DECL_CHUNK_EX(sub_0202FBCC, sub_0202FBD4)` plus 4 gExtraSaveChunkHeaders entries (idx 2-5) casting them through (SAVESIZEFN)/(SAVEINITFN) -- per insights.md 'save-chunk-ipa-safe', do NOT modify save_arrays.c or replace the macro; leave it as forward-declared externs coexisting with the new header.

Encrypt/decrypt seed construction must match exactly: seed = chk | ((chk ^ 0xFFFF) << 16) where chk is the raw u16 checksum -- this exact idiom recurs 3x in the file (sub_0202FC90, sub_0202FD28, sub_02030814) and must be reproduced literally, not algebraically simplified, to match MWCC codegen.

sub_020302A4 and sub_020304F0 are large mirror-image field-copy functions (~20 raw offset reads/writes each) with only medium/low confidence on exact field semantics -- high risk of NONMATCHING on register allocation per the project's idx-stride-cse and adjacent-field-store-forces-reload insights; consider decompiling in small chunks with frequent objdiff checks.

notes: This file implements the 'Battle Hall' battle-facility save-chunk subsystem: a single struct type (UnkStruct_0202FBCC, 0x1D50 bytes) registered 4 times in src/save_arrays.c's gExtraSaveChunkHeaders (chunk indices 2-5, presumably one per difficulty/rank tier), with a process-global pointer (_021D2AF8) holding whichever instance is currently loaded into memory. The struct itself layers a sentinel header (0x0), a LinkBattleRuleset-derived ruleset block (0x4, 0x80 bytes), a CRC-checked descriptor block (0x84, 0x64 bytes), and an encrypted payload (0xe8, 0x1C64 bytes) containing 4 challenger trainer records (party + profile snapshots) plus an Options struct. Functions break into clean groups: load/save/free lifecycle (sub_0202FBCC/FBD4/FBF0/FC24/FC48/FC5C/FC74/FC90/FD28/FDA4/FE14), CRC/format validators (sub_02030154/0203018C), per-battler encrypted-log byte accessors (sub_02030260/0203027C, already header-declared and caller-confirmed), bulk save<->work-buffer field copiers (sub_020302A4/020304F0/020306DC/02030724), simple sub-block extractors/duplicators (sub_0203077C/020307AC/020307DC/020307F8/02030814/02030920/02030938/02030940), and a generic field get/set dispatcher pair for the per-record struct (sub_02030978/02030A24, plus the odd dual-return sub_0203088C). All 33 distinct imported symbols already have prototypes in existing headers (heap.h, save.h, player_data.h, pokedex.h, options.h, party.h, pokemon.h, link_ruleset_data.h, system.h, math_util.h, error_handling.h, save_arrays.h, unk_02030A98.h, nitro/mi/memory.h, sound_chatot.h), so no new import signatures need to be guessed from scratch -- the main remaining work is internal struct-field naming and the IPA-safe header split.
